full_judgment:
In this civil revision at the instance of the returned candidate the questions that fall for my determination are whether the Tribunal below committed error in law in holding 114 ballot papers cast in favour of the petitioner invalid and whether the petitioner stands disqualified for contesting in the election of the local Union Parishad for the post of Chairman. 

 4. Mr. Shahidul Islam submits that the Presiding Officer as on counting the votes sealed the same and put into separate bags as per Rule 38 of the Union Parishad (Election) Rules, 1983 there was no violation of these Rules. It is also argued that as on counting the votes the petitioner was found to secure the highest votes he was declared elected chairman and there was no tampering with the ballot papers. He submits that the appellate Court and the Tribunal failed to consider that the gunny bags containing the ballot papers were not intact and this indicates that there was some mischief done by somebody in tampering with the ballot papers. Mr. Fazlul Karim, on the other hand, submits that the finding that 114 ballot papers were invalid based on evidence. He submits that both the Tribunal and the Appellate Court found that there was no tampering with the ballot papers. 

 5. Rule 38 of the Union Parishad (Election) Rules, 1983 provides for counting of votes. Clause (b) of sub-rule (3) of rule 38 provides for separation of the invalid ballot papers, Mr. Karim placed reliance upon clause (v) to contend that 114 ballot papers containing double seals have to be declared invalid, Read clause (v) of sub-rule (3) of rule 38 with R. 40(1) (a) it seems to me that 114 ballot papers containing such marks are invalid ballot papers.
